svg.text: Two Funnels, A Fork, A Loop
A funnel of psychological temptations converges on 'pareidolia', a funnel of four technical arguments converges on
'functionalism is shaky', that uncertainty forks into two distinct ethical risks, and the close loops back to the
opening question of what makes us us.

g.text: The essay funnels psychological biases into 'pareidolia', funnels four technical arguments into 'functionalism looks
shaky', forks the resulting uncertainty into two live ethical risks, then loops back to the human question it opened

g.title: Does AI consciousness matter? — With consciousness comes moral status, rights, and the risk of suffering — for AI and for us. — → spya-e68t9h
Human-centered biases — anthropocentrism, exceptionalism, anthropomorphism — Three overlapping biases make us project mind onto anything humanlike. — → spya-cvaqgs
Fluent language feels human — Saying chatbots 'hallucinate' quietly implies they experience things. — → spya-k6fpme
Techno-hype & rapture dreams — Exponential growth and Promethean ambition make imminent machine minds feel inevitable. — → spya-cke6sj
Pareidolia, not evidence — Seeing consciousness in AI may be like seeing a face in a cinnamon bun. — → spya-k850tu
Brains aren't computers — No clean software/hardware split exists in living neural tissue. — → spya-sk4su6
More than algorithms — Analogue, continuous, dynamical processes may matter beyond Turing computation. — → spya-affgsh
Life may be necessary — Consciousness may be tied to self-sustaining, living, metabolic processes. — → spya-e7jqx4
Simulating ≠ creating — A simulated storm doesn't get anything wet; a simulated brain may not feel. — → spya-cqh5wq
Functionalism looks shaky — Four independent arguments converge, though none is a knock-down proof. — → spya-uzr60x
Deep uncertainty remains — No one can say for sure what would create, or avoid, real machine consciousness. — → spya-yverz7
Don't deliberately create conscious AI — Doing so risks introducing new moral subjects and new suffering at scale. — → spya-e7fdmb
Conscious-seeming AI is already here — Illusory consciousness poses its own distinct, present-day ethical risks. — → spya-vs0vpj
Recovering an embodied sense of self — More breath than thought, more meat than machine — a return to what makes us us. — → spya-zv36xq
g.text: Recovering an embodied sense of self
WHY WE'RE TEMPTED TO SEE IT
One conflation (intelligence with consciousness) opens two parallel tracks — cognitive bias, and hype — that both
funnel into the same conclusion: this looks like pattern-seeing, not evidence.

g.title: Intelligence isn't consciousness — Intelligence is about doing; consciousness is about being — they needn't travel together. — → spya-nh8mt7
Anthropocentrism — Taking the human case as definitional rather than as one example among many. — → spya-h4mwb2
Exceptionalism & anthropomorphism — Putting humans atop every pile, then projecting our qualities onto lookalikes. — → spya-her4zk
Language feels most human — LLMs pull our psychological strings via speech in a way AlphaFold never does. — → spya-k6fpme
'Hallucinate' implies feeling — Better to say AI 'confabulates' — a doing word, not an experiencing one. — → spya-t29n67
Exponential growth feels urgent — On an exponential curve every point feels like an inflection point. — → spya-cke6sj
Techno-rapture: silicon immortality — The Promethean lure of god-like creation and escape from decaying bodies. — → spya-v4sduf
Seeing consciousness like faces in toast — Recognizing the pareidolia is only the first step, not the whole answer. — → spya-k850tu

g.text: The assumed premise (computation suffices) is challenged by four independent arguments, two of them carrying a specific
worked example, all converging on the same verdict.

g.title: Assumes computation = consciousness — Computational functionalism is the load-bearing assumption behind conscious AI. — → spya-wepmnr
Brains aren't computers — No clean split between wetware and mindware, unlike hardware and software. — → spya-sk4su6
More than algorithms — Continuous, stochastic, dynamical processes lie outside Turing computation. — → spya-affgsh
Life may be necessary — Predictive self-regulation ties conscious feeling to living, metabolizing bodies. — → spya-e7jqx4
Simulating ≠ creating — A simulation of digestion digests nothing; a simulated brain may feel nothing. — → spya-cqh5wq
Neuron swap fails — can't replace with silicon — Chalmers' replacement thought experiment fails at its first hurdle. — → spya-ahtr6e
Needs same assumption — Bostrom's hidden premise — The simulation hypothesis quietly assumes a program can be conscious. — → spya-bcnvp2
Functionalism looks shaky — Not disproof — but four independent lines all point the same way. — → spya-uzr60x
